# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — openpyxl-in-place + compute-from-data + mandatory inspect/verify
- Changes I made (file · cluster):
  - prompt.md · METHOD: mandate openpyxl `load_workbook`→write target cells by coordinate→`save`; forbid `df.to_excel` for writing (it drops other sheets, adds a header row that shifts data, appends a new column, reparses text→datetime/number). Targets the pandas-round-trip cluster (168-17, 188-39, 52532, 53449, 438-18-flaky).
  - prompt.md · CONTRACT: rewrote the old "prefer literals" line into "compute each answer cell from the data the code reads — never hardcode a preview value," with the 3-copy-replay rationale. Kept LITERAL output. Targets non-generalizing/hardcoded answers (43213 wrote 0.0; 47766 hardcoded 2023).
  - prompt.md · CONTRACT: explicit type rule (number-as-number, float where fractional, text stays text, no new/renamed columns, no writing past the answer's last row, guard None source cells). Targets 43213/56915/438-18 type mismatches.
  - task_template.md · STRUCTURE: made INSPECT the unavoidable first step (print sheets, headers, column letters, data extent — locate the table dynamically). Targets guessed-coordinate failures (188-39 KeyError→no file, 52532, 53449, 56915).
  - task_template.md · STRUCTURE: pre-finish checklist — may reply with no code ONLY after re-opening output and confirming value+type+nothing-outside-changed+sheets-present. Targets the re-paste-and-stop-unverified pattern (all).
  - both files · rule: every reply = exactly one ```python block, reasoning as `#` comments. Targets wasted `<think>`-only first turns (160-6, 47766, 52532, 53449 t0).
- Expected effect + safety: converts pandas-corruption 0s (168-17, 188-39, 52532, 53449) and hardcoded-value 0s (43213) toward passing; makes flaky 160-6/438-18 more consistent (438-18's failing trial was pandas datetime reparse — openpyxl removes it). SAFE: 0 solid tasks exist; edits are additive or method/contract changes that don't flip the delete-row/value-replace behavior of the two flaky tasks.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none — iteration 1, empty LEDGER/JOURNAL. Used memory `libreoffice-recalc-active`.
- Refuted-by-memory (did NOT try): switching the answer to LIVE FORMULAS. Recalc is grading-side only; the agent's in-sandbox verify uses `data_only=True` with no recalc, so a formula reads back None and defeats the verification checklist, and it's an unbounded flip of "prefer literals" that risks literal-passing tasks. Kept literals + compute-in-code instead.
- High-value clusters still not cracked: 47766 (SUMIFS year-boundary reasoning) and 56915 (INDEX/MATCH over merged-cell DATA sheet) are hard even with the method fix; did not hardcode (would overfit).
- Plateau signal: n/a (first iteration).
- Focus next iteration: if accepted, read RESULT to see which of the 7 zeros moved; if 47766/56915 remain, consider a worked example of the specific idiom (SUMIFS with date criteria / INDEX-MATCH with a header-row lookup) rather than more general prose. If rejected, check whether mandatory-INSPECT cost too many turns and relax it to "inspect unless coordinates are already certain."

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.244 Δ=+0.096 · fixed={—} · broke={—} · unresolved={160-6} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them).
<!-- cand_0001: ACCEPTED val=0.244 Δ=+0.096 -->

## Iteration cand_0002 — force INSPECT-first + make the final block self-contained (stop the read-only-verify replay trap)
- Changes I made (1 line per edit; file + cluster):
  - E1 task_template.md · STRUCTURE (ordered precondition): rewrote the 3 steps → TURN 1 = INSPECT ONLY (print sheets/headers/column-letters/data-extent/cells around answer_position, MUST NOT save); TURN 2+ = ONE self-contained block load-input→compute→save→read-back-print. Targets the "steps listed but never executed" cluster on ALL failing tasks (49945 wrong criterion col, 43213 wrong avg col, 52532 header off-by-one, 188-39/56915 merged headers).
  - E2 prompt.md §grading · CONTRACT (sourced rule): the replay hands the final block only the input file + empty output location, so it must load spreadsheet_path→compute→save output_path by itself; a read-only reopen-output block scores 0. Targets 168-17.
  - E3 prompt.md §working-rules · CONSOLIDATE: replaced the parent's "a verification turn re-opens output_path" line (which CAUSED 168-17) with "verify inside the same self-contained block; never a later output-only reply."
  - E4 prompt.md new §"Locate the data before you compute" · KNOWLEDGE/worked pitfalls: right column (key col ≠ raw col), right rows (top rows are headers, write below), merged cells (value only in top-left; unmerge/forward-fill), write only what is asked (group/pivot → label group rows, not every raw row). Targets 49945/43213 (col), 52532/438-18 (rows), 56915/188-39 (merged), 53449 (over-fill).
- Expected effect + why safe: converts the guess-and-save 0s toward passing by forcing the model to SEE the real layout (E1/E4) and by making the final graded block always self-contained (E2/E3), which also stabilizes flaky 168-17 (read-only final block was its only failure mode) and 438-18 (header offset + read-back). SAFE: only ONE passing task, 160-6, whose winning block was already self-contained load-input→delete→save; the inspect turn + read-back print do not change its saved output, and it triggers none of the E4 pitfall conditions.
- Building on prior RESULTS: built on cand_0001 (ACCEPTED +0.096) — KEPT its openpyxl-in-place method, compute-from-data, and type contract (broke nothing, so nothing to drop). cand_0001 left the residual problem that its INSPECT/VERIFY steps were listed but skipped; this iteration attacks that with STRUCTURE, not more emphasis.
- Refuted hypotheses (do not re-test): switching to live formulas — in-sandbox verify has no recalc so a formula reads back None and defeats the read-back check (recorded by cand_0001). Kept literals-computed-in-code.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: 47766 (3-block SUMIFS over a date range) and the two-key merged-cell match in 56915/188-39 have a real reasoning component beyond inspection; added knowledge to help but did NOT hardcode task logic. If this iteration is accepted but they stay at 0, the next lever is a worked EXAMPLE of the exact idiom (multi-range SUMIFS; forward-fill-then-two-key-INDEX/MATCH) rather than more general prose.
- Plateau signal: only 2 iterations so far, both additive on the same capability; not yet a plateau. If cand_0002 is rejected, the likely culprit is E1's UNBOUNDED procedure rewrite costing turns or perturbing 160-6 — in that case keep E2/E3/E4 (all BOUNDED/additive) and soften E1 to "inspect first unless the layout is already certain."
- Focus next iteration: read the RESULT to see which of the 7 zeros moved; if the merged-cell/multi-range tasks remain, ship the worked-idiom examples.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.233 Δ=-0.011 · fixed={—} · broke={—} · unresolved={160-6, 168-17, 438-18} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them). — no task that was passing under the parent regressed: this batch did not clear the gate's threshold, it did not do damage. So the lever is POWER or SIZE, not a redesign — re-measure with more trials in ONE evaluation, or make the effect bigger. Keep the edits that produced the `fixed` tasks above as your starting point; do not rewrite them on this round's numbers.
<!-- cand_0002: rejected val=0.233 Δ=-0.011 -->

<!-- cap-evolve:journal-append-below — add your Iteration entry under this line; do not edit anything above it -->

## Iteration cand_0003 — worked-example lever for "read the wrong place" + self-contained final block + real verify
- Changes I made (file · cluster):
  - prompt.md · WORKED EXAMPLE (new lever): one end-to-end template — paste literal paths, read a
    data_only copy, PRINT the full extent, key each target row on the label BESIDE it, aggregate the raw
    column over ws.max_row, write a computed literal, save a normally-loaded workbook, read back. Targets
    the modal "read the wrong column/row/extent" cluster: 49945 (key col F not C), 43213 (data in col A
    not B), 52532 (header off-by-one), 47766 (assumed bounds/block).
  - prompt.md · KNOWLEDGE: "instruction coords = user intent, not layout"; row 1 is a header; keys sit
    beside the target; aggregate the FULL extent; read cached values via a SEPARATE data_only copy while
    the SAVE workbook stays normal (global data_only load+save would corrupt untouched formula cells).
  - prompt.md · CONTRACT: self-contained final block; DELETED the champion's harmful "a verification turn
    re-opens output_path" line (it CAUSES 168-17's 2/3-copy failure); verify now inside the saving block.
  - prompt.md · CONTRACT: write the computed LITERAL, never an Excel formula string (can't self-verify
    in-sandbox; all-or-nothing on recalc). Targets 47766/49945 formula trials.
  - prompt.md · path fix: state spreadsheet_path/output_path are literal TEXT, not predefined variables
    (NameError burned turns in 47766/188-39/168-17/438-18).
  - task_template.md · STRUCTURE: INSPECT only counts if it PRINTS; VERIFY = read the SAVED file back +
    assert plausibility (all-zero/None/identical ⇒ wrong column, fix). Targets fake-verify (43213 t2
    ignored [0,0,0,0]).
  - task_template.md · KNOWLEDGE: sheet-level fill = key-lookup not positional join (188-39); answer_position
    is a maximum not a quota, grouped/summary answers fill fewer cells (53449 over-filled 12/15).
- Expected effect + safety: E2/E3 verified against GOLD (all 3 variants) to reproduce 49945, 43213, 52532
  exactly → these 3 zeros should move; E1 makes flaky 168-17 (and partly 438-18) consistent. SAFE: only
  passer 160-6 is a self-contained deletion task that triggers none of the conditional aggregation/lookup/
  grouping rules, writes no formula, and its read-back is filled data (no plausibility false-alarm).
- Building on prior RESULTS: built on cand_0001 (ACCEPTED +0.096) — kept its openpyxl-in-place, compute-
  from-data, and type contract (broke nothing). cand_0002 (REJECTED, broke nothing, Δ-0.011) had the right
  direction (inspect + self-contained) but too little POWER; framework said "make the effect bigger, not a
  redesign." So I re-add the self-contained fix (E1) and deliver the inspect/locate fix as a concrete
  WORKED EXAMPLE (bigger lever for a weak reader) rather than cand_0002's prose pitfalls + rigid turn-role
  rewrite (which I did NOT re-try — it was the suspected UNBOUNDED edit).
- Refuted hypotheses (not re-tested): live formulas as the answer (memory: no in-sandbox recalc ⇒ reads
  None, can't verify; all-or-nothing on grading regressed lookups in another run).
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: 56915 (merged-cell cross-sheet two-key lookup) — needs multi-step
  reasoning beyond inspection; gave inspect-merged + key-beside-target guidance but no task logic (would
  overfit). 43213 expanding-window + 52532 tie semantics rely on the model following the located data.
- Plateau signal: 2 iterations, 1 accept 1 reject; noise is large (2·SE≈0.17 on n=10×3), so a real gain
  needs ~2 full task fixes. Lever switched this round from prose/structure to a VERIFIED worked example.
- Focus next iteration: read RESULT; if 49945/43213/52532 moved, the worked-example lever is confirmed —
  extend it with a second example for the merged-cell / cross-sheet key-lookup shape (56915/188-39). If
  rejected with no movement, the weak reader is likely ignoring the example too → the ceiling may be model
  capability, not prompt; record that and stop tuning prose.
